latin.491: GAR. Etsi saepius peccatum originale, inhaerens in visceribus hominum, nomine ἡ ἁμαρτία designat Apostolus, non est tamen necessarium, ut ubicumque vocabulum illud usurpat, intelligatur id peccatum: quod facile agnoscet, qui Paulum legerit de peccato loquentem, Rom. VI. 2. 6. 23: 2. Cor. 15. 56: 2. Thess. 2. 3. Heb. XII. 4.
latin.492: PLAC. Haec prima mea ratio non est mea, sed maximi viri, Bezae, quem Vir doctus per latus meum ferit. Vide sis eius Annot. ad Rom. 5. 12. Per peccatum eo loco id intelligo, quod Calvinus, Beza, Martyr, aliique eiusmodi primae notae Theologi, intellexerunt, à quibus caeteri, qui me innovatae doctrinae accusant, discedunt: quod ne pateret, mentionem Bezae, eiusque verba, unde nervus & robur argumenti pendebat, (adeo quidem ut vix apud Paulum addito articulo aliud declaret,) alto silentio Vir doctus praeteriit.
latin.493: Non enim ex eo argumentor, quod ἁμαρτία eo nomine peccatum inhaerens Apostolus designet, sed quod tam saepe, ut vix unquam aliud addito articulo declaret, hic autem additur articulus. Quis vero nescit, usitatissimam significationem anteponendam esse rarissimae, nisi forte gravis impediat ratio, quae hic nulla apparet, aut à viro docto affertur. Imo quae exempla affert, ea rationem nostram confirmant potius quam evertunt: in eis enim locis peccati nomine inhaerens vitium vel solum, vel cum fructibus suis intelligitur.
latin.494: GAR. 2. Cum imputatio primi peccati, & corruptio haereditaria, sint ἀχώριστα, etiam hic peccati nomine, ex vi consequentiae, intelligi posse corruptionem illam, non inficiamur. PLAC. Si essent ἀχώριστα, quandiu manet corruptio, tandiu maneret imputatio: id quod cum omnium Theologorum sententia, quotquot non sunt Pelagiani, pugnat. Tollitur enim imputatio remissione peccati originalis, quae fit, non ut ne sit, sed ut ne imputetur amplius. Quod si peccati quod per unum hominem introiit in mundum nomine corruptio haereditaria intelligitur, quo argumento probabunt illi, qui nobis in hac causa adversantur, peccatum actuale intelligi quod nostrum non sit factum nisi per imputationem? Nam intelligendum esse peccatum inhaerens & nomen ἁμαρτία cum articulo, & maximorum theologorum autoritas, & confessio Adversariorum satis confirmant.
latin.495: Secundam rationem mihi suppeditant verba sequentia, εἰς τὸν κόσμον εἰσῆλθε in mundum introiit. Per mundum autem omnes homines intelligi cum tu & fere omnes interpretes fateamini, nihil opus est probare. Sic igitur ratiocinor, Peccatum, quod per Adamum in omnes homines introiit, non est peccatum actuale Adami, sed corruptio haereditaria. Atqui Apostolus loquitur de peccato quod per Adamum in omnes homines introiit. Ergo loquitur non de peccato actuali Adami, sed de corruptione haereditaria.
latin.496: Minor est liquida. Maior quomodo negari possit non video. Constat enim & convenit inter nos per Adamum corruptionem haereditariam quae vere peccatum est in omnes homines ingressam esse: quo posito, quid est quamobrem de ea non accipiamus Apostoli verba?

pass_a.491: GAR: Granted Paul often marks original sin inhering in human entrails by ἡ ἁμαρτία—still not every use must mean that sin. Anyone who has read Paul on sin (Rom 6:2, 6, 23; 2 Cor 15:56; 2 Thess 2:3; Heb 12:4) sees the range.
pass_a.492: PLAC: My first stroke is not mine but Beza's—the learned man wounds me through his side. See his Annot. on Rom 5:12. By sin there I take what Calvin, Beza, Martyr, and first-rank theologians of that stamp took—from whom those who charge me with novelty depart. Lest that show, the learned man passed Beza's name and the very words that were the nerve and strength of the argument (scarcely anything else in Paul with the article) in deep silence.
pass_a.493: I do not argue merely that ἁμαρτία can name inhering sin, but that it does so so often that with the article it scarcely ever marks anything else—and here the article is added. Prefer the usual sense to the rarest unless a grave reason blocks it; none appears, nor does he offer one. His own examples confirm us more than they overturn us: there 'sin' means inhering vice alone or with its fruits.
pass_a.494: GAR 2: Since first-sin imputation and hereditary corruption are inseparable (ἀχώριστα), we do not deny that here too, by consequence, the name of sin can mean that corruption. PLAC: If inseparable, imputation would last as long as corruption—against every non-Pelagian theologian. Remission lifts imputation not by making the sin cease to be, but by making it no longer imputed. And if the entered-sin's name is hereditary corruption, what still proves the actual that is ours only by imputation? That inhering sin and articular ἁμαρτία are meant is confirmed by the greatest theologians' authority and even the adversaries' confession.
pass_a.495: Second reason: the next words—εἰς τὸν κόσμον εἰσῆλθε, entered into the world. You and nearly all interpreters grant 'world' = all humans; no proof needed. So: the sin that entered through Adam into all is not Adam's actual but hereditary corruption; Paul speaks of that entered-sin; therefore not of Adam's actual but of hereditary corruption.
pass_a.496: The minor is clear. How the major could be denied I do not see. We agree that through Adam hereditary corruption—which is truly sin—entered into all humans: that granted, why not take the Apostle's words of it? Tip before GAR Cap. VII § IX (actual by reatus).

491: GAR. Although the Apostle more often designates original sin, inhering in the entrails of humans, by the name he hamartia, it is nevertheless not necessary that wherever he uses that word, that sin be understood: which anyone will easily recognize who has read Paul speaking of sin, Rom. VI. 2. 6. 23: 2. Cor. 15. 56: 2. Thess. 2. 3. Heb. XII. 4.
492: PLAC. This my first reason is not mine, but of a most great man, Beza, whom the learned man strikes through my side. See if you will his Annot. on Rom. 5. 12. By sin in that place I understand what Calvin, Beza, Martyr, and other theologians of first note of that kind understood, from whom the rest, who accuse me of innovated doctrine, depart: which lest it lie open, mention of Beza, and his words, from which the nerve and strength of the argument hung, (so much so that scarcely in Paul with the article added does it declare anything else,) the learned man passed by in deep silence.
493: For I do not argue from this, that by that name hamartia the Apostle designates inhering sin, but that so often, that scarcely ever with the article added does it declare anything else, and here the article is added. But who does not know that the most usual signification is to be preferred to the rarest, unless perhaps a grave reason blocks it, which here appears none, or is brought forward by the learned man. Nay, the examples he brings confirm our reason rather than overturn it: for in those places by the name of sin inhering vice either alone, or with its fruits, is understood.
494: GAR. 2. Since the imputation of the first sin, and hereditary corruption, are inseparable, even here we do not deny that by the name of sin, by force of consequence, that corruption can be understood. PLAC. If they were inseparable, as long as corruption remains, so long would imputation remain: which fights with the opinion of all theologians, as many as are not Pelagians. For imputation is taken away by the remission of original sin, which is done, not so that it may not be, but so that it may no longer be imputed. But if by the name of the sin which entered into the world through one man hereditary corruption is understood, by what argument will those who oppose us in this cause prove that actual sin is understood which was not made ours except by imputation? For that inhering sin must be understood, and the name hamartia with the article, both the authority of the greatest theologians, and the adversaries' confession, sufficiently confirm.
495: A second reason the following words supply me, eis ton kosmon eiselthe, entered into the world. But that by the world all humans are understood, since you and almost all interpreters confess it, there is no need to prove. I reason therefore thus: The sin which entered through Adam into all humans is not Adam's actual sin, but hereditary corruption. But the Apostle speaks of the sin which entered through Adam into all humans. Therefore he speaks not of Adam's actual sin, but of hereditary corruption.
496: The Minor is clear. How the Major could be denied I do not see. For it is agreed and convenes between us that through Adam hereditary corruption which is truly sin entered into all humans: which being posited, what is there why we should not take the Apostle's words of it?
